Convert external data containers to iconic_data

Source: R/iconic_data.R, R/mae.R
as_iconic_data.Rd

S3 generic bridging other data interfaces to the estimation interface. Methods:

Usage

as_iconic_data(input, ...)

# Default S3 method
as_iconic_data(input, ...)

# S3 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
as_iconic_data(
  input,
  assay = 1,
  mediator_assay = NULL,
  exposure,
  instrument = NULL,
  mediator_instrument = NULL,
  negative_controls = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  surv_time = NULL,
  surv_event = NULL,
  bin_outcome = NULL,
  outcome_type = c("continuous", "survival", "binary"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'MultiAssayExperiment'
as_iconic_data(
  input,
  exposure,
  outcome = NULL,
  mediator = NULL,
  instrument = NULL,
  mediator_instrument = NULL,
  negative_controls = NULL,
  W1 = NULL,
  W2 = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  surv_time = NULL,
  surv_event = NULL,
  bin_outcome = NULL,
  outcome_type = c("continuous", "survival", "binary"),
  assay = 1L,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

input

An object to convert: a MultiAssayExperiment, a SummarizedExperiment, a list returned by load_real_input_data(), an iconic_data object, or an exposure vector (named-argument form).

...

Named arguments passed to iconic_data() when using the named-argument form, or to the method.

assay

SummarizedExperiment method: name or index of the assay of input holding the outcome panel (features x samples). Default 1. Set to NULL for survival outcomes (when surv_time/surv_event are colData columns and no continuous outcome panel is used). MultiAssayExperiment method: name or index of the assay used within each SummarizedExperiment experiment. Default 1.

mediator_assay

Optional name or index of an assay holding the mediator panel (mediators x samples).

exposure

Character: name of the colData column holding the exposure X (MultiAssayExperiment method: or of a single experiment). For the MultiAssayExperiment method, when exposure is missing and input was produced by as_MultiAssayExperiment(), the roles recorded in metadata(input)$iconic are used (round trip).

instrument

Optional character: name of the colData column holding the exposure instrument G (e.g. a polygenic score).

mediator_instrument

Optional character vector of colData column names holding the mediator instrument(s) Gm (one column per mediator); for the MultiAssayExperiment method, alternatively the name of an experiment (instruments x samples).

negative_controls

Optional character vector of colData column names forming the negative-control panel W; for the MultiAssayExperiment method, alternatively the name of an experiment (e.g. principal components from build_w_pcs(), features x samples).

covariates

Optional character vector of colData column names to carry through as covariates.

surv_time, surv_event

Optional character: names of colData columns holding follow-up time and the 0/1 event indicator; set together with outcome_type = "survival".

bin_outcome

Optional character: name of a colData column holding the 0/1 outcome; set together with outcome_type = "binary".

outcome_type

\"continuous\" (default), \"survival\", or \"binary\".

outcome

For the MultiAssayExperiment method: name of the experiment holding the outcome panel Y (features x samples). Required when outcome_type = "continuous".

mediator

Optional: name of the experiment (or character vector of colData columns) holding the mediator panel M.

W1, W2

Optional: names of experiments (or character vectors of colData columns) holding the path-specific negative-control panels for the X->M (W1) and M->Y (W2) paths.

verbose

Logical: report samples dropped during alignment. Default TRUE.

Value

An iconic_data S3 object.

Details

  • default: a list returned by load_real_input_data(), an existing iconic_data object (returned as-is), or the exposure vector X with named arguments matching iconic_data() (Y, M, G, Gm, W, W1, W2, covariates, feature_names, mediator_names), which delegates to iconic_data().

  • MultiAssayExperiment (recommended for multi-omic data): omics panels (outcome, mediator, negative controls, mediator instruments) are experiments, sample-level fields (exposure, instrument, covariates, survival / binary outcome) are colData columns, and samples are matched through the sampleMap. See Details and as_MultiAssayExperiment() for the reverse conversion.

  • SummarizedExperiment: extracts the outcome panel from an assay and sample-level fields (exposure, instruments, negative controls, covariates) from colData.

MultiAssayExperiment method. Each role (outcome, mediator, negative_controls, W1, W2, mediator_instrument, and optionally exposure / instrument) names either one experiment of input or one or more colData columns; experiment names take precedence. For SummarizedExperiment experiments the assay selected by assay is used; matrix experiments are used directly. Samples are matched through sampleMap(input) to primary IDs (the rownames of colData). Only primaries present in every experiment used, and with non-missing values in the sample-level colData columns used, are kept. Experiments with more than one column per primary (e.g. technical replicates) must be collapsed first, for example with MultiAssayExperiment::mergeReplicates(). The aligned components are passed to iconic_data(), so validation and scaling are identical to calling it directly.

Examples

# From a load_real_input_data() result
input <- load_real_input_data(example = TRUE)
data <- as_iconic_data(input)
#> Warning: W has 30 features but Y has 1. Using row recycling.
print(data)
#> <iconic_data> 200 samples, 1 outcome features
#>  Available: W (negative controls), W1/W2 (path-specific NCs) 
#>  Covariates: sex, GA, mother_ethnicity_indian, mother_ethnicity_malay 
#>  Mode: total effect 

# From named components (delegates to iconic_data())
data <- as_iconic_data(rnorm(100), Y = matrix(rnorm(100 * 10), 10, 100),
    G = rnorm(100), Gm = rnorm(100),
    W = matrix(rnorm(100 * 10), 10, 100))
se <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
    assays = list(expr = matrix(rnorm(20 * 60), 20, 60,
        dimnames = list(paste0("gene", 1:20),
            paste0("S", 1:60)))),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        bmi = rnorm(60), prs = rnorm(60),
        nc1 = rnorm(60), nc2 = rnorm(60), age = rnorm(60))
)
data <- as_iconic_data(se, assay = "expr", exposure = "bmi",
    instrument = "prs",
    negative_controls = c("nc1", "nc2"),
    covariates = "age")
#> Warning: W has 2 features but Y has 20. Using row recycling.
print(data)
#> <iconic_data> 60 samples, 20 outcome features
#>  Available: G (exposure instrument), W (negative controls), W1/W2 (path-specific NCs) 
#>  Covariates: age 
#>  Mode: total effect 
# From a MultiAssayExperiment: omics panels are experiments,
# sample-level variables are colData columns
set.seed(1)
ids <- paste0("S", 1:80)
mk <- function(p, pre) matrix(rnorm(p * 80), p, 80,
    dimnames = list(paste0(pre, seq_len(p)), ids))
mae <- MultiAssayExperiment::MultiAssayExperiment(
    experiments = list(
        rna = SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
            assays = list(expr = mk(10, "gene"))),
        methyl = SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
            assays = list(m = mk(1, "cg"))),
        nc = SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
            assays = list(pcs = mk(10, "PC")))),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        bmi = rnorm(80), prs = rnorm(80), cis_score = rnorm(80),
        age = rnorm(80), row.names = ids))
data <- as_iconic_data(mae, exposure = "bmi", outcome = "rna",
    mediator = "methyl", instrument = "prs",
    mediator_instrument = "cis_score", negative_controls = "nc",
    covariates = "age")
print(data)
#> <iconic_data> 80 samples, 10 outcome features, 1 mediator(s)
#>  Available: G (exposure instrument), Gm (mediator instrument), W (negative controls), W1/W2 (path-specific NCs) 
#>  Covariates: age 
#>  Mode: mediation
